counting: Launch attempts, returned calls and validated calls are counted separately for build, helper and aiken calls. Every returned raw call, including rejected helper and build outputs, is appended to result.calls BEFORE parsing or validation. Staging copies are pure Python data movement, counted as no native call. Cargo/rustc subprocesses inside the single build are transitive effects of that launch, never one native operation.
entropy: Phase A: exactly two helper calls (one per scheme); each call draws exactly two 32-byte entropy reads (escrow key first, seller key second), creates both keys only inside the helper process, signs each signer's own message once, and dies with the process. The scheme token is validated before any entropy is opened, so a malformed argument consumes no key attempt. An invalid scalar from either draw fails the whole invocation with no redraw and no entropy retry. Secret scalars are never stored, printed or serialized; entropy buffers are zeroed best-effort with no memory-erasure theorem claimed. Ephemeral test keys are not future live catalogue keys. The existing Ed25519 wallet is never read and no wallet/key/PK/SRS/provercache or /w path is ever stat'ed, read, hashed or walked.

producerContract: Producer output format moriarty-vi-signer-producer-output/2 carries, per scheme, exactly two intents in signer order escrow, seller. Each intent's limits are the gold-true facts: escrow authorizes gross 37 (fee 2 + transfer 35), fee cap 2, beneficiary seller, closing liability cap 69 (residual invoice 55 + reserve 14); seller (invoice discharge creditor) authorizes zero debit with beneficiary seller. The adapter fails closed unless the producer program_hash equals the gold parsed-program hash and both rebuilt Aiken messages equal the Core signing_messages byte-for-byte. The producer core_verify value is reported internal agreement only and is never trusted as external verification.

signingRoutes.chosen: High-level k256 Signer::try_sign on each exact Core signing_message (escrow and seller messages) for both schemes. Core verify_intent uses the matching Verifier::verify(message), and VI supplies sha2_256(message) to the Cardano builtin, so one signature per signer serves both consumers.
signingRoutes.programDerivation: mori_core::parse on the exact pinned installment-invoice.mori bytes (parse also validates), then prepare_intent. No hand-written Program/Action/expression/statement exists anywhere in the helper, and no duplicated transcription of the .mori source is embedded; only frozen identity guards (source hash, parsed names, request scenario values, gold program hash) are embedded, and any mismatch refuses before signing.
signingRoutes.rejectedDoubleHash: Passing the 32-byte digest to Signer would apply a second outer SHA-256 and fail Core verification.
signingRoutes.rejectedPrehash: Passing the full message to sign_prehash/sign_raw, or signing the digest with a prehash API that guesses auxiliary randomness, is refused: Schnorr uses zero auxiliary bytes and ECDSA uses deterministic RFC6979 through the high-level Signer.
